units.text: INT. HUSBAND - CONTINUOUS
Oh! I hope you are not going to leave me all alone with Lord Goring? Especially at such an early hour in the day.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: I am afraid I can’t take him with me to Downing Street. It is not the Prime Minster’s day for seeing the unemployed.
units.name: LORD CAVERSHAM

units.text: Shakes hands with MABEL CHILTERN, takes up his hat and stick , and goes out , with a parting glare of indignation at LORD GORING.
Takes up roses and begins to arrange them in a bowl on the table .
People who don’t keep their appointments in the Park are horrid.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: Detestable.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: I am glad you admit it. But I wish you wouldn’t look so pleased about it.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: I can’t help it. I always look pleased when I am with you.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Sadly .
Then I suppose it is my duty to remain with you?
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: Of course it is.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Well, my duty is a thing I never do, on principle. It always depresses me. So I am afraid I must leave you.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: Please don’t, Miss Mabel. I have something very particular to say to you.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Rapturously .
Oh! is it a proposal?
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: Somewhat taken aback .
Well, yes, it is—I am bound to say it is.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: With a sigh of pleasure .
I am so glad. That makes the second to-day.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: Indignantly .
The second to-day? What conceited ass has been impertinent enough to dare to propose to you before I had proposed to you?
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Tommy Trafford, of course. It is one of Tommy’s days for proposing. He always proposes on Tuesdays and Thursdays, during the Season.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: You didn’t accept him, I hope?
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: I make it a rule never to accept Tommy. That is why he goes on proposing. Of course, as you didn’t turn up this morning, I very nearly said yes. It would have been an excellent lesson both for him and for you if I had. It would have taught you both better manners.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: Oh! bother Tommy Trafford. Tommy is a silly little ass. I love you.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: I know. And I think you might have mentioned it before. I am sure I have given you heaps of opportunities.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: Mabel, do be serious. Please be serious.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Ah! that is the sort of thing a man always says to a girl before he has been married to her. He never says it afterwards.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: Taking hold of her hand .
Mabel, I have told you that I love you. Can’t you love me a little in return?
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: You silly Arthur! If you knew anything about . . . anything, which you don’t, you would know that I adore you. Every one in London knows it except you. It is a public scandal the way I adore you. I have been going about for the last six months telling the whole of society that I adore you. I wonder you consent to have anything to say to me. I have no character left at all. At least, I feel so happy that I am quite sure I have no character left at all.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: Catches her in his arms and kisses her .
Then there is a pause of bliss .
Dear! Do you know I was awfully afraid of being refused!
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Looking up at him .
But you never have been refused yet by anybody, have you, Arthur? I can’t imagine any one refusing you.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: After kissing her again .
Of course I’m not nearly good enough for you, Mabel.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Nestling close to him .
I am so glad, darling. I was afraid you were.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: After some hesitation .
And I’m . . . I’m a little over thirty.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: Dear, you look weeks younger than that.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN

units.text: Enthusiastically .
How sweet of you to say so! . . . And it is only fair to tell you frankly that I am fearfully extravagant.
units.name: LORD GORING

units.text: But so am I, Arthur. So we’re sure to agree. And now I must go and see Gertrude.
units.name: MABEL CHILTERN
